subject: Feasibility: capacity decomposition + role matrix for NimbleHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nimblehealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Jane Porter <jane.porter@nimblehealth.com>, procure@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment interest + high-level requirements

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NimbleHealth is interested in a VPC/private deployment for our PII/PHI use case. To move forward we need a clearer breakdown of the capacity and the internal roles Red wood would expect us to cover vs. what you provide.

High-level asks from our side:
- Expected GPU footprint for ~100 concurrent inference sessions (average prompt length ~800 tokens)
- Network topology and egress expectations for a HIPAA-like environment
- What of the operational runbook is customer-managed vs Redwood-managed (backups, patching, KMS integration)
- Security questionnaire: we attached the form we prefer filled out (we can accept a response matrix)

Can you share a simple decomposition and who on Redwood will need to be involved during onboarding and steady-state? We are on a tight Q4 timeline.

Regards,
Rajiv
VP of Product, NimbleHealth

Attachment: nimble_security_questionnaire.pdf (uploaded)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment interest + high-level requirements

Irene — quick architecture notes and capacity decomposition below (high level). I kept this intentionally compact for the one-pager.

1) Capacity assumptions (Nimble inputs): 100 concurrent sessions, avg prompt 800 tokens, avg generation 200 tokens, P99 response latency target <500ms.

2) GPU footprint (approx):
- Baseline inference cluster: 4x A800 (or equivalent L40S) per availability zone for active serving with batching and KV cache enabled.
- Hot standby (cross-AZ): 1x A800 per AZ for failover.
- Total recommended GPUs: 12 A800s (3 AZs x 4 active + 3 x 1 standby) — this tolerates AZ loss and provides headroom for bursts.
- If they accept 1s P99 and higher batching, we could reduce to 8 A800s.

3) Network/topology notes:
- Hybrid setup: customer VPC peered to Redwood-managed subnets via PrivateLink or Transit Gateway. No public internet egress for inference traffic.
- Egress: model downloads and telemetry only (TLS 1.3) — recommend explicit allowlist for model repo endpoints.

4) Operational split (brief):
- Redwood provides: inference runtime, model binaries and version pinning, runtime patching windows, automated KV cache priming guidance, and incident escalation to infra SRE.
- Customer provides: VPC peering, KMS/HSM endpoint and key policy, internal network ACLs, and first-line on-prem networking ops.

5) Estimated onboarding compute-days: 6 infra engineer days for initial provisioning + 8 engineer-days for validation and load testing (Marcus-led).

6) Quick cost delta note: Private (12x A800) roughly 2.8x per-token cost vs hosted for this workload (main drivers: reserved capacity overhead and cross-AZ redundancy). We should include a sensitivity table in the attachment.

I'll attach a simple network diagram and the capacity estimate spreadsheet.

-- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_nimble_network_diagram.png, vpc_capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment interest + high-level requirements

Adding SRE/resourcing perspective. Key points:

- Onboarding support model: 2x platform engineers for first 4 weeks (on-call rotation during onboarding), then 0.2 FTE platform SRE ongoing for maintenance and upgrade windows (we handle runtime critical patches).
- Runbook handoffs: we need their networking and KMS contacts scheduled for at least two 90-min sessions (design + test).
- Incident escalation: Redwood retains Tier 2 for runtime; customer must maintain Tier 1 for network/host reachability.
- Estimated ongoing support burn (steady-state): ~32 hours/month of platform/SRE time for telemetry/patching/quarterly upgrades per deployment.

Operational dependencies that could slow project:
- Procurement lead time for cross-account Transit Gateway or PrivateLink approvals (customer side).
- KMS/HSM certs — we may need to accept their HSM vendor or arrange an integration lead; that typically adds 2–3 weeks.

Irene: tallying these into the role matrix (who owns what, and who schedules which sessions).

-Rishi
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment interest + high-level requirements

Irene — a few legal/procurement flags to surface before we commit to timelines:

1) KMS/HSM language: if they require Redwood to hold or import keys on their behalf in customer HSM, we need an exhibit and minimum indemnity language. If it's customer-managed KMS with cross-account access, that's a standard integration.
2) Data residency & logs: confirm whether audit logs will reside in customer account or we export copies. If Nimble requires audit log retention policies beyond our standard retention, that will be an added cost.
3) SLA/credits: Private deployments are eligible for SLA but also require nonstandard acceptance criteria — propose we offer a tailored SLA once committed capacity and regions are agreed.

Please ask procurement to capture their expected contract milestone dates (PO, SOC attestation, compliance onboarding). If Nimble wants SOC2 evidence, we can provide our latest report but may need a time box for extra evidence collection.

-Laura
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment interest + high-level requirements — next steps and role matrix (draft)

Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two short artifacts: a 1-page capacity decomposition (vpc_capacity_estimate.xlsx) and a one-page role matrix + gating checklist. Summary below:

Summary highlights:  
- Recommended baseline: 12x A800s across 3 AZs (see sensitivity tab for 8x option).
- Expected onboarding effort from Redwood: ~14 engineer-days (platform + validation) and 2x engineers allocated during the first 4 weeks for operational handover.
- Operational split: Redwood manages runtime, upgrades, and incident escalation; Nimble provides VPC peering, KMS/HSM endpoints, and first-line network ops.
- Legal/procurement: Laura flagged potential HSM indemnities and audit log retention items.

Draft role matrix (who schedules initial session):
- Redwood: Marcus (network design session), Rishi (onboarding runbook & SRE rota), Laura (contract template & SOC evidence), Irene (product onboarding owner)
- Nimble: Rajiv (product sponsor), Jane Porter (CISO/infosec contact), procure@nimblehealth.com (contracting)

Gating checklist:
- KMS integration decision (customer-managed vs Redwood brokered) — action: Jane / Nimble (by 2027-09-12)
- Network provisioning approvals for PrivateLink/Transit GW — action: Nimble procurement (by 2027-09-15)
- Contract milestone (PO + security exhibit) — action: Redwood legal + Nimble procurement (TBD)

Next step: propose a 60-min cross-functional kickoff Wednesday 2027-09-08 10am PT to walk the diagram and confirm timelines. Please let me know availability.

Thanks — attaching the files and the filled security questionnaire for their records.

Irene Choi
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
